title: observability: add token-level tracing spans, dashboards, and alert SLO adjustments
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: operators and SREs need finer-grained visibility into per-token latency and cost attribution to diagnose regressions (esp. tail latency caused by batching and KV cache behavior) and to tune alerts/SLOs. This PR adds token-level tracing spans, new Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboard panels for token-cost/latency breakdown, and alert tuning for token-generation SLOs. Changes are backwards-compatible (no breaking public API) and include a rollout plan with canary, metrics-only first, and toggle for tracing to limit overhead. Highlights: add tracing spans at token emit points, emit token_generation_latency and token_generation_cost metrics, aggregate per-route/token-type dashboards, add alert rules with adjusted thresholds and burn-rate windows, update console dashboards and docs, add integration tests and CI checks. Rollout: 1) deploy metrics-only change to canary; 2) enable tracing for 5% traffic for 24h and validate overhead; 3) full enable with monitoring. Related: ENG-2489, ENG-2498, PM-134.
commits_summary: 6 commits: telemetry: add token spans and proto fields; metrics: new counters/histograms for token latency/cost; grafana: dashboard JSON with token breakdown panels; alerts: tuned token-generation SLO rules; console: dashboard panels + UX for token cost breakdown; tests: e2e telemetry integration and perf smoke. Commits include unit tests and small refactors for telemetry interfaces.
review_comments: Eliot Chen (reviewer): Nice work. A few questions: what's the expected CPU overhead when tracing is enabled at 100%? Can we gate spans behind a sampling config?

Sofia Patel (author): We measured ~2-4% CPU increase at 100% traffic in our perf lab for a medium model with token spans enabled. Tracing is gated behind telemetry.token_span_sampling and can be enabled at 0.01/0.1/1.0. Added config docs and a flag to turn off for Dedicated instances.
Priya Singh (reviewer): Alert thresholds look stricter than current SLOs; do we want an initial monitoring period before enforcing?

Sofia Patel (author): Yes - alerts were added as "monitoring" mode initially (severity: info) for the first week in prod canary. Updated alert annotations to include runbook links and monitoring-only signal.
Lena Gomez (approver): Approved after small nits on naming and an added unit test for histogram labels.
release_notes: Adds token-level tracing spans and metrics; new Grafana dashboard panels for token cost and latency breakdown; adjusted token-generation SLO alerts (initially monitoring-only). Operators can enable/disable token-span tracing via telemetry.token_span_sampling. Performance overhead measured ~2-4% CPU at 100% sampling in perf lab.
testing: Unit tests for new metrics and histogram labels; e2e telemetry integration test validates metrics flow from runtime -> exporter -> Prometheus; perf smoke pipeline added to detect overhead regressions; manual canary run documented in PR description.
notes_for_ops: 1) Metrics names are token_generation_latency_seconds_bucket, token_generation_cost_cents_total, token_cache_hit_rate; 2) Alerts initially in monitoring mode - change severity to page after 7d if stable; 3) Console dashboard wiring requires 1 migration job to populate route metadata; migration safe and reversible.
changelog_entry: Observability: token-level metrics/tracing, dashboards, and alert tuning (monitoring mode)
